artifact.title: Torrent File — Full-Detail Knowledge Graph
artifact.subject: BitTorrent .torrent meta-info file format
artifact.description: Detailed machine-readable graph of torrent-file structure, metadata fields, v1/v2 identity and integrity models, extensions, discovery methods, workflow, examples, limitations, and source references.
artifact.source_policy: Primary descriptive claims are grounded in the user-provided Torrent file article text. General security implications are explicitly identified as inference where applicable.

entities.name: Torrent file
entities.description: A .torrent meta-info file containing metadata that describes distributed content and how a BitTorrent client can discover peers.

entities.name: application/x-bittorrent
entities.description: Internet media type associated with .torrent files.

entities.name: BEP-0003
entities.description: BitTorrent v1 protocol specification defining the classic torrent metadata model and protocol behavior.

entities.name: BEP-0052
entities.description: BitTorrent v2 specification introducing a revised metadata layout, SHA-256-based hashing, file trees, and Merkle-based integrity metadata.

entities.name: Metadata
entities.description: Descriptive information about files and directories, including names, sizes, paths, piece layout, integrity hashes, and discovery hints.

entities.name: Content payload
entities.description: The actual files or folders being distributed; the torrent file describes them but does not itself contain their payload bytes.

entities.name: Torrent as table of contents
entities.description: The torrent metadata acts as an index that lets a client understand the content layout and locate data pieces across peers.

entities.name: Peer-to-peer distribution
entities.description: Distribution model in which participating clients exchange pieces directly rather than requiring every client to fetch all bytes from a central server.

entities.name: Swarm
entities.description: The group of peers participating in distribution of content identified by a torrent.

entities.name: Peer
entities.description: A BitTorrent participant that can request pieces and, after obtaining them, typically make those pieces available to other participants.

entities.name: Seeder
entities.description: A peer that has the complete content and continues uploading pieces to other peers.

entities.name: Piece
entities.description: A logical chunk of content independently requested and integrity-checked in the classic BitTorrent model.

entities.name: 16 KiB block
entities.description: A 16 KiB data block used as a leaf-level input in the BitTorrent v2 Merkle construction described by the article.

entities.name: announce
entities.description: Top-level field containing a tracker URL in the classic metadata structure.

entities.name: announce-list
entities.description: Top-level extension field containing multiple tracker tiers or URLs.

entities.name: info dictionary
entities.description: Dictionary containing core content identity and layout metadata; the info dictionary is the input used to calculate the torrent infohash.

entities.name: name
entities.description: Suggested file name for a single-file torrent or suggested directory name for a multi-file torrent.

entities.name: length
entities.description: File length in bytes; used directly for single-file torrents and inside each file entry for multi-file torrents.

entities.name: files list
entities.description: List of per-file dictionaries used when a torrent describes multiple files.

entities.name: path
entities.description: List of path components that identifies a file within the multi-file torrent's directory structure.

entities.name: piece length
entities.description: Number of bytes represented by each piece; v2 requires this value to be a power of two.

entities.name: pieces
entities.description: In v1, concatenated binary SHA-1 hashes for the pieces; the byte string length is a multiple of 20 bytes.

entities.name: Bencoding
entities.description: The encoding used for torrent metadata dictionaries, lists, integers, and byte strings; dictionary keys are lexicographically ordered.

entities.name: UTF-8
entities.description: String values are UTF-8 encoded, except the v1 pieces field, which is binary hash data.

entities.name: v1 infohash
entities.description: SHA-1 digest calculated over the bencoded info dictionary; identifies the torrent in v1 peer discovery and magnet links.

entities.name: SHA-1
entities.description: 160-bit hash function used by the classic v1 pieces field and v1 infohash.

entities.name: SHA-256
entities.description: Hash function used in BitTorrent v2 piece-integrity metadata and the v2 infohash.

entities.name: v2 infohash
entities.description: SHA-256-based identifier for a v2 torrent's info dictionary; the full hash is represented in btmh magnet links.

entities.name: Magnet link
entities.description: A link that identifies a torrent through its content hash and allows a client to acquire metadata without first downloading a .torrent file.

entities.name: meta version
entities.description: Field with value 2 identifying the v2 metadata format.

entities.name: file tree
entities.description: Tree of dictionaries whose keys represent directory or file names in the v2 metadata layout.

entities.name: piece root
entities.description: For a non-empty v2 file, the Merkle root associated with the file's integrity tree built from 16 KiB blocks.

entities.name: piece layers
entities.description: Dictionary holding Merkle root hash data for pieces in the v2 format.

entities.name: Merkle tree
entities.description: Hash tree in which child hashes are combined recursively to produce a root hash that can support integrity proofs and localized verification.

entities.name: Integrity verification
entities.description: Checking downloaded content against hashes committed to by torrent metadata; this establishes data integrity relative to the metadata, not safety or legitimacy.

entities.name: Tracker
entities.description: A service named by torrent metadata that helps clients discover peers participating in a swarm.

entities.name: Distributed hash table (DHT)
entities.description: A decentralized peer-discovery mechanism; BitTorrent Mainline DHT is specified by BEP-0005.

entities.name: BEP-0005
entities.description: BitTorrent extension for distributed hash tables, specifically Mainline DHT.

entities.name: nodes
entities.description: Optional bootstrap node list used by trackerless torrent metadata; entries pair host names or addresses with ports.

entities.name: Trackerless torrent
entities.description: A torrent that omits announce and instead can include nodes for DHT bootstrap information.

entities.name: BEP-0012
entities.description: Multitracker metadata extension adding announce-list to support multiple trackers.

entities.name: Multiple trackers
entities.description: Providing multiple tracker endpoints can offer alternative peer-discovery paths if a tracker is unavailable.

entities.name: BEP-0019
entities.description: Extension that adds url-list web-seed URLs usable by clients to retrieve ordinary HTTP data without special server-side support.

entities.name: url-list
entities.description: Top-level list of URLs used as web seeds under BEP-0019.

entities.name: Web seed
entities.description: An HTTP(S) source from which a BitTorrent client can retrieve content alongside peer-to-peer sources.

entities.name: BEP-0017
entities.description: Extension defining the httpseeds field for web addresses where data can be retrieved with special server support; article describes it as Draft status.

entities.name: httpseeds
entities.description: List of web addresses for retrieving torrent data using the BEP-0017 approach, which requires special server support according to the article.

entities.name: BEP-0027
entities.description: Private torrents extension defining a private flag in the info dictionary.

entities.name: private
entities.description: Flag with value 1 indicating a private torrent policy; the article says decentralized discovery mechanisms are disabled to preserve tracker control.

entities.name: Private tracker
entities.description: Tracker that restricts access to its peer list, often by recognizing registered users or known IP addresses and maintaining transfer statistics.

entities.name: Peer Exchange (PEX)
entities.description: A decentralized peer-discovery method that private-torrent policy typically disables according to the article.

entities.name: Local Service Discovery (LSD)
entities.description: A local-network peer-discovery method that private-torrent policy typically disables according to the article.

entities.name: BEP-0030
entities.description: Extension describing Merkle hash torrents intended to reduce torrent metadata size; the article describes a root_hash field and SHA-1-based construction.

entities.name: root_hash
entities.description: Legacy Merkle-torrent field containing a binary SHA-1 Merkle root in the BEP-0030 description.

entities.name: Hybrid torrent
entities.description: Torrent metadata that carries both v1-compatible and v2 fields so clients can support both ecosystems; v1 and v2 identities differ and clients must merge corresponding swarms.

entities.name: Single-file torrent
entities.description: Torrent whose info dictionary uses length to describe one file.

entities.name: Multi-file torrent
entities.description: Torrent whose info dictionary uses a files list with per-file length and path fields.

entities.name: Piece boundaries across files
entities.description: In the classic multi-file model, file data is concatenated in files-list order for piece hashing; pieces are generally piece-length sized except the last.

entities.name: Piece count
entities.description: Number of pieces for a classic torrent is ceiling(total content bytes / piece length), with the last piece possibly shorter.

entities.name: Binary hash blob
entities.description: The v1 pieces field is a binary byte string rather than human-readable UTF-8 text.

entities.name: Hash security limitation
entities.description: The article characterizes SHA-1 as broken in the v2 comparison; v2 adopts SHA-256 for integrity metadata and infohashing.

entities.name: Torrent metadata size
entities.description: The size of a .torrent file is influenced by metadata and the amount of integrity-hash information it carries; Merkle approaches can reduce metadata burden in described cases.

entities.name: Server load reduction
entities.description: Peer-to-peer piece exchange distributes outbound bandwidth demand across participants instead of requiring one source to serve every copy.

entities.name: Asymmetric internet access
entities.description: Many access connections provide greater download than upload capacity, which can constrain centralized distribution and motivate peer-to-peer sharing.

entities.name: BitTorrent client
entities.description: Software that parses torrent metadata, discovers peers, requests and verifies pieces, assembles content, and may continue uploading after completion.

entities.name: Metadata acquisition
entities.description: A user obtains a .torrent file directly or begins from a magnet link and then uses a client to obtain the necessary metadata and content.

entities.name: Piece assembly
entities.description: After all pieces have been obtained and verified, the client reconstructs the usable file or directory structure.

entities.name: Private flag is not cryptographic privacy
entities.description: The private flag is a tracker-policy signal, not a guarantee of anonymity; manually removing it changes the infohash and creates a different swarm.

entities.name: Tracker list excluded from infohash
entities.description: Changes to fields outside the info dictionary, such as the tracker list, do not change the infohash; changes inside info do.

entities.name: Truncated v2 hash for legacy message structures
entities.description: The article states that tracker and DHT communication use a 20-byte truncated v2 hash while btmh magnet links carry the full 32-byte hash.

entities.name: btmh
entities.description: Magnet-link topic type that carries the full 32-byte v2 SHA-256-based hash.

entities.name: Cross-torrent duplicate-file detection
entities.description: Independent per-file Merkle roots in v2 can allow duplicate files to be recognized across torrents even when piece lengths differ.

entities.name: Empty file
entities.description: A zero-length file does not have the non-empty-file piece root described by the v2 format.

entities.name: Linux distribution delivery
entities.description: Open-source operating systems and Linux distributions may offer torrent downloads to spread distribution bandwidth across users.

entities.name: Mirror site
entities.description: An alternate HTTP(S) source that can be combined with peer-to-peer sources for robust delivery.

entities.name: Content legitimacy
entities.description: Torrent metadata and hashes do not establish whether content is lawful, authorized, or safe to execute.

entities.name: Malware risk
entities.description: A hash match establishes consistency with torrent metadata but does not prove downloaded files are benign.

architecture_patterns.name: Parse and interpret a v1 .torrent file
architecture_patterns.summary: Decode bencoding, read the info dictionary, interpret single-file or multi-file layout, and use piece hashes to verify payload chunks.

steps.action: Read the .torrent byte stream and decode its bencoded top-level dictionary.
Read announce if present, plus optional extension fields such as announce-list, url-list, httpseeds, nodes, and private.
Read info.name and either info.length for a single file or info.files entries for a multi-file torrent.
Read piece length and split the logical content stream into pieces; multi-file v1 content follows files-list order.
Interpret pieces as concatenated 20-byte SHA-1 digests, one digest per piece.
Calculate the v1 infohash over the exact bencoded info dictionary and use it for torrent identity.
Use trackers and/or DHT to discover peers, fetch pieces, verify them, and assemble the payload.

architecture_patterns.name: BitTorrent v2 metadata and Merkle verification
architecture_patterns.summary: Use v2 metadata fields and SHA-256-based Merkle structures to describe files and verify content at block and piece levels.

steps.action: Identify v2 metadata using meta version = 2.
Read file tree to determine the directory and file hierarchy.
Read piece length, which must be a power of two in v2.
For each non-empty file, interpret piece root as the Merkle root built from 16 KiB blocks.
Use piece layers to carry per-piece Merkle root data.
Use SHA-256-based piece hashing and v2 infohashing; use the full hash in btmh magnet links.
When speaking to legacy tracker/DHT message structures, account for the described 20-byte truncated hash.

architecture_patterns.name: Trackerless discovery via DHT
architecture_patterns.summary: Omit the announce tracker field and include optional DHT bootstrap nodes, allowing peer discovery through a distributed hash table.

steps.action: Represent a trackerless torrent without an announce key.
Optionally include nodes as host/port pairs, ideally useful nearby routing-table nodes or a known reliable node.
Client uses Mainline DHT to discover peers for the torrent identity.
Client connects directly to discovered peers and participates in the swarm.

architecture_patterns.name: Combine peers, trackers, and web seeds
architecture_patterns.summary: Use multiple peer-discovery endpoints and optional HTTP(S) web seeds to improve availability and reduce pressure on any single distribution server.

steps.action: Include announce-list with multiple tracker URLs when supported.
Optionally include url-list web-seed URLs.
Client discovers peers through trackers and/or DHT as permitted by torrent policy.
Client fetches pieces from peers and web seeds, combining sources where supported.

architecture_patterns.name: Private torrent discovery policy
architecture_patterns.summary: Use the private flag and a private tracker to enforce a community-controlled peer-discovery convention, while recognizing that the flag is not anonymity.

steps.action: Set info.private to 1.
Use a private tracker that gates peer-list access.
Disable DHT, PEX, and LSD in compliant clients to preserve tracker control.
Do not treat this flag as encryption or anonymity; modifying the info dictionary changes the infohash.

architecture_patterns.name: Hybrid v1/v2 compatibility
architecture_patterns.summary: Carry old and new metadata fields to support both v1 and v2 clients, while managing distinct v1 and v2 infohash identities.

steps.action: Include v1-compatible and v2 metadata structures in the hybrid torrent.
Compute the corresponding v1 and v2 infohashes.
Recognize that distinct identities may produce separate swarms in the respective networks.
Use client logic to associate and merge the corresponding v1 and v2 swarm participation.

architecture_patterns.name: Separate integrity from trust and safety
architecture_patterns.summary: Use metadata hashes to detect corruption or mismatch, but do not infer that a file is safe, lawful, or trustworthy solely because its hashes match.

steps.action: Verify downloaded pieces or blocks against hashes in the torrent metadata.
Treat successful verification as evidence that bytes match the metadata's committed hashes.
Assess source trust, file behavior, and legal authorization separately.

derived_rules.statement: For v1, the pieces byte string length is a multiple of 20 bytes because each SHA-1 digest is 160 bits.
Piece count for a non-empty classic content stream is the ceiling of total content bytes divided by piece length.
BitTorrent v2 requires piece length to be a power of two.
Infohash identity is computed from the bencoded info dictionary; changing fields outside info such as announce does not affect it, while changing info does.
The v2 Merkle tree described by the article is constructed from 16 KiB blocks.

caveats: This is a knowledge graph derived primarily from the supplied article, not a replacement for the current normative BEP specifications.
The source article itself notes citation and cleanup issues, including extension status labels that may be outdated.
The source's displayed piece-length expression has formatting corruption; the intended example value is 256 KiB = 262144 bytes.
The graph preserves the article's descriptions of BEP status rather than independently updating each status.
A successful hash check verifies consistency with torrent metadata; it does not prove that content is benign, lawful, or trustworthy.
